==国史において== 『[[続日本後紀]]』によると[[承和 (日本)|承和]]9年（[[842年]]）5月に「信濃国諏方郡無位勲八等南方刀美神」の[[神階]]が[[従五位|従五位下]]に、続いて同年10月に「信濃国無位健御名方富命前八坂刀売神」が同じく従五位下に昇格された。それから上社の建御名方神と同様にかなり急速に昇位するが、上社のほうが一歩先に進むというあり方が見られる宮坂光昭「強大なる神の国―諏訪信仰の特質」『御柱祭と諏訪大社』筑摩書房、1987年、37-38頁。{{Cite web|和書|url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/240101.html|author=|title=南方刀美神社二座（信濃国諏方郡）|website=21世紀COEプログラム「神道・神社史料集成」|publisher=國學院大學|date=|accessdate=2019-01-20}}。 *[[嘉祥]]3年（[[850年]]）10月15日「信濃国御名方富命神・健御名方富命前八坂刀売命神、並加'''従五位上'''」（『[[日本文徳天皇実録|文徳実録]]』） *[[仁寿]]元年（[[851年]]）10月27日「進信濃国建御名方富命・前八坂刀売命等両大神階、加'''従三位'''」（『文徳実録』） *[[貞観 (日本)|貞観]]元年（[[859年]]）1月27日「信濃国正三位勲八等建御名方富命神'''従二位'''、従三位建御名方富命前八坂刀売命神'''正三位'''」（『[[日本三代実録|三代実録]]』） *同年2月11日「授信濃国従二位勲八等建御名方富命神'''正二位'''、正三位建御名方富命前八坂刀売命神'''従二位'''」（『三代実録』） *貞観9年（[[867年]]）3月11日「信濃国正二位勲八等建御名方富命神進階'''従一位'''、従二位建御名方富命前八坂刀自命神'''正二位'''」（『三代実録』） 諏訪上社・下社の急速な神階上昇は当時大活躍していた[[金刺氏]]（[[科野国造]]の一族、後の下社大祝家）の大きな力があったと考えられる諏訪市史編纂委員会 編「第二節 諏訪神社上社・下社」『諏訪市史 上巻 (原始・古代・中世)』1995年、697頁。宮坂光昭 『諏訪大社の御柱と年中行事』 郷土出版社、1992年、12-13頁。。 ==考証== ===下社の起源=== [[ファイル:Shimosuwa Aozuka Kofun zenkei.JPG|サムネイル|[[下諏訪青塚古墳]]]] 諏訪下社は6世紀末から7世紀初頭に[[伊那郡]]から[[諏訪郡|諏訪]]や[[埴科郡|埴科]]、[[水内郡|水内]]へ進出した金刺氏が創建したものと考えられている。 金刺氏の祖の墓と想定されている[[下諏訪青塚古墳|青塚古墳]]は下社秋宮の近辺に位置しているため、秋宮は自ずから祖先祭祀の場で、[[砥川 (長野県)|砥川]]のほとりにある下社春宮は、水霊を祀る祭場だったと思われる。要するに、[[諏訪湖]]の北に拠点を構えた金刺氏はその王墓を祀り（秋宮）、砥川の自然信仰（春宮）を取り込み、諏訪下社となる社壇を作り上げた寺田鎮子、鷲尾徹太『諏訪明神―カミ信仰の原像』岩田書院、2010年、69-70頁。。 [[ファイル:Megamihōri-no-in (売神祝印) seal imprint.png|left|サムネイル|90px|
売神祝印
]]諏訪上社が主祭神を男神とし、そして後裔の大祝に男性を即位させたのに対して、下社側が祭神を女性として神話を持たせたと推測される宮坂光昭 『諏訪大社の御柱と年中行事』 郷土出版社、1992年、13頁。。宮坂光昭（1987年）は、「ヤサカトメ」という神名が元々水稲農耕における豊作呪術をよくする[[巫女]]（かんなぎ）の名称であり、これが後に下社の女神に当てられたという説を提唱した。実際には下社の神事は農耕関係のものが多い。 ===下社の祭神=== [[平安時代]]の初め頃には既に下社に女神が祀られていることは[[平城天皇]]より下賜されたといわれる「{{読み仮名|売神祝|めがみほうり}}印」の存在から窺える{{Cite web|和書|title=売神祝ノ印|url=http://www.town.shimosuwa.lg.jp/www/contents/1001000000748/index.html|website=下諏訪町公式ホームページ|access-date=2018-01-21}}。なお、中世以降には混乱が生じ、下社の祭神に建御名方神、[[片倉辺命]]、[[事代主神]]、[[沼河比売|沼河姫]]、もしくは[[シタテルヒメ|下照姫]]をあてる文書はいくつかある{{efn|事代主神が上社、建御名方神が下社の祭神とする場合もある。}}。現在は八坂刀売神とともに建御名方神が主祭神となっており、事代主神が配祀されている『日本の神々―神社と聖地〈9〉美濃・飛騨・信濃』 谷川健一、白水社、1987年、140頁。。 [[ファイル:Suwa Taisha Maemiya Burial Place (諏訪大社 前宮 本殿横神陵伝承地).jpg|175px|サムネイル|
神陵伝承地（上社前宮）
]] ===八坂刀売神と前宮=== 現在、八坂刀売神は下社のほかに上社{{読み仮名|前宮|まえみや}}の祭神ともされているが、これは国史に見られる「前八坂刀売神」の「{{読み仮名|前|きさき}}」を「まえ」と読まれたことから生じた誤りである宮坂光昭「強大なる神の国―諏訪信仰の特質」『御柱祭と諏訪大社』筑摩書房、1987年、38頁。。古文献からは、前宮の本来の祭神は「二十の御社宮神（[[ミシャグジ]]）」であることがわかる北村皆雄「「ミシャグジ祭政体」考」『古代諏訪とミシャグジ祭政体の研究』古代部族研究会編、人間社、2017年、105-127頁。 山本ひろ子「諏訪学の構築のために 序論にかえて」 『諏訪学』 国書刊行会、2018年、45-47頁。。 なお、前宮の本殿の横には、タケミナカタまたはヤサカトメの墓（神陵）と伝わる塚がある『長野県の地名』諏訪大社上社前宮神殿跡項。。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} === 注釈 === {{Notelist}} === 出典 === {{Reflist|30em}} == 参考文献・サイト == ; 書籍 * {{Cite book|和書|author=上田正昭 他|authorlink=上田正昭|year=1987|title=御柱祭と諏訪大社|publisher=[[筑摩書房]]|isbn=978-4-480-84181-0|ref={{Harvid|御柱祭と諏訪大社|1987年}}}} * [[太田亮]]『[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/983470 諏訪神社誌 第1巻]』、官幣大社諏訪神社附属諏訪明神講社、1926年。 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=諏訪市史編纂委員会|year=1995|title=諏訪市史 上巻 (原始・古代・中世)|ncid=BN02906048|publisher=諏訪市|ref={{Harvid|諏訪市史|1995年}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=福田晃|others=二本松康宏、徳田和夫|year=2015|title=諏訪信仰の中世―神話・伝承・歴史|publisher=三弥井書店|isbn=978-4-838-23288-8|ref={{Harvid|諏訪信仰の中世|2015年}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|author=宮坂光昭|year=1992|title=諏訪大社の御柱と年中行事|publisher=郷土出版社|isbn=978-4-876-63178-0|ref={{Harvid|諏訪大社の御柱と年中行事|1992年}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|author=宮地直一|authorlink=宮地直一|year=1931|title=[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1076393 諏訪史 第2巻 前編]|publisher=信濃教育会諏訪部会|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|諏訪史 第2巻 前|1931年}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|author=宮地直一|year=1937|title=[https://books.google.co.jp/books?id=UHYSgY4lTZcC 諏訪史 第2巻 後編]|publisher=信濃教育会諏訪部会|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|諏訪史 第2巻 後|1937年}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=谷川健一|year=1987|title=日本の神々―神社と聖地〈9〉美濃・飛騨・信濃|publisher=白水社|isbn=978-4-560-02509-3}} ; サイト * {{Cite web|和書|url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/240101.html|author=|title=南方刀美神社二座（信濃国諏方郡）|work=|publisher=國學院大學21世紀COEプログラム「神道・神社史料集成」|date=|accessdate=2016-1-8|ref={{Harvid|神道・神社史料集成}}}} == 関連項目 == * [[タケミナカタ|建御名方神]] * [[天白神]] * [[諏方大明神画詞]] * [[安曇氏]] {{神道 横}} {{諏訪信仰}} {{DEFAULTSORT:やさかとめのかみ}} [[Category:日本の神]] [[Category:諏訪信仰|神やさかとめ]]

[[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q9150392]] Wikidata name: Yasakatome [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:29, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Japanese deity}} {{Expand Japanese|八坂刀売神}} {{Infobox deity | type = Deity ([[Kunitsukami]], Senior First Rank) | name = Yasakatome
{{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|qid=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|qid=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|qid=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|qid=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. Stories and claims about the goddess are diverse and contradictory. Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼). As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. Stories and claims about the goddess are diverse and contradictory. Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼). Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. [[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q9150392]] Wikidata name: Yasakatome [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:29, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Japanese deity}} {{Expand Japanese|八坂刀売神}} {{Infobox deity | type = Deity ([[Kunitsukami]], Senior First Rank) | name = Yasakatome
{{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|WD=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|WD=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. Stories and claims about the goddess are diverse and contradictory. Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼). [[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q9150392]] Wikidata name: Yasakatome [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:29, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Japanese deity}} {{Expand Japanese|八坂刀売神}} {{Infobox deity | type = Deity ([[Kunitsukami]], Senior First Rank) | name = Yasakatome
{{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|WD=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|WD=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. Stories and claims about the goddess are diverse and contradictory. Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼). Gakuseisha. p. 48, cited in Kanai (1982). p. 6. == See also == *{{ill|Takeminakata|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeminakata|qq=}} * {{ill|Tenshirakami|ja|天白神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenshirakami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天白信仰|1=Tenpaku faith|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3616095}} * {{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|qq=}} * [[Azumi people]] ==References== {{reflist}} == Bibliography == {{refbegin|30em|qq=draft}} *{{cite book |last=Ashkenazi |first=Michael |url=https://archive.org/details/handbookofjapane0000ashk |title=Handbook of Japanese Mythology |date=2003 |publisher=ABC-CLIO |isbn=978-1-57607-467-1 |url-access=registration}} *{{cite book |last1=Aston |first1=George |url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Nihongi:_Chronicles_of_Japan_from_the_Earliest_Times_to_A.D._697 |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697 |date=1896 |publisher=Kegan Paul, Trench, Trübner & Co. |location=London}} *{{cite book |last1=Chamberlain |first1=Basil (trans.) |url=http://sacred-texts.com/shi/kj/index.htm |title=A Translation of the "Ko-Ji-Ki," or "Records of Ancient Matters" |date=1882 |publisher=Lane, Crawford & Co. |location=Yokohama}} *{{cite book |title=諏訪信仰の中世―神話・伝承・歴史 (Suwa shinkō no chūsei: shinwa, denshō, rekishi) |date=2015 |publisher=Miyai Shoten |isbn=978-4838232888 |editor1-last=Fukuda |editor1-first=Akira |editor2-last=Nihonmatsu |editor2-first=Yasuhiro |editor3-last=Tokuda |editor3-first=Kazuo}} {{in lang|ja}} *{{cite thesis |type=PhD |last1=Grumbach |first1=Lisa |title=Sacrifice and Salvation in Medieval Japan: Hunting and Meat in Religious Practice at Suwa Jinja |date=2005 |publisher=Stanford University}} *{{cite book |author=J. {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|WD=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|WD=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. Stories and claims about the goddess are diverse and contradictory. Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼). B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. [[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q9150392]] Wikidata name: Yasakatome [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:29, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Japanese deity}} {{Expand Japanese|八坂刀売神}} {{Infobox deity | type = Deity ([[Kunitsukami]], Senior First Rank) | name = Yasakatome
{{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|WD=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|WD=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. Stories and claims about the goddess are diverse and contradictory. Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. [[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q9150392]] Wikidata name: Yasakatome [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:29, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Japanese deity}} {{Expand Japanese|八坂刀売神}} {{Infobox deity | type = Deity ([[Kunitsukami]], Senior First Rank) | name = Yasakatome
{{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|WD=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|WD=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. Stories and claims about the goddess are diverse and contradictory. Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼). [[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q9150392]] Wikidata name: Yasakatome [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:29, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Japanese deity}} {{Expand Japanese|八坂刀売神}} {{Infobox deity | type = Deity ([[Kunitsukami]], Senior First Rank) | name = Yasakatome
{{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|WD=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|WD=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. Stories and claims about the goddess are diverse and contradictory. Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼). Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼). {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|WD=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|WD=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. A. [[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q9150392]] Wikidata name: Yasakatome [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:29, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Japanese deity}} {{Expand Japanese|八坂刀売神}} {{Infobox deity | type = Deity ([[Kunitsukami]], Senior First Rank) | name = Yasakatome
{{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|WD=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|WD=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. Stories and claims about the goddess are diverse and contradictory. Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼).
