[[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q9150392]] Wikidata name: Yasakatome [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:29, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Japanese deity}} {{Expand Japanese|八坂刀売神}} {{Infobox deity | type = Deity ([[Kunitsukami]], Senior First Rank) | name = Yasakatome
{{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|WD=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|WD=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. Stories and claims about the goddess are diverse and contradictory. Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼). Gakuseisha. p. 48, cited in Kanai (1982). p. 6. == See also == *{{ill|Takeminakata|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeminakata|qq=}} * {{ill|Tenshirakami|ja|天白神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenshirakami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天白信仰|1=Tenpaku faith|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3616095}} * {{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|qq=}} * [[Azumi people]] ==References== {{reflist}} == Bibliography == {{refbegin|30em|qq=draft}} *{{cite book |last=Ashkenazi |first=Michael |url=https://archive.org/details/handbookofjapane0000ashk |title=Handbook of Japanese Mythology |date=2003 |publisher=ABC-CLIO |isbn=978-1-57607-467-1 |url-access=registration}} *{{cite book |last1=Aston |first1=George |url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Nihongi:_Chronicles_of_Japan_from_the_Earliest_Times_to_A.D._697 |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697 |date=1896 |publisher=Kegan Paul, Trench, Trübner & Co. |location=London}} *{{cite book |last1=Chamberlain |first1=Basil (trans.) |url=http://sacred-texts.com/shi/kj/index.htm |title=A Translation of the "Ko-Ji-Ki," or "Records of Ancient Matters" |date=1882 |publisher=Lane, Crawford & Co. |location=Yokohama}} *{{cite book |title=諏訪信仰の中世―神話・伝承・歴史 (Suwa shinkō no chūsei: shinwa, denshō, rekishi) |date=2015 |publisher=Miyai Shoten |isbn=978-4838232888 |editor1-last=Fukuda |editor1-first=Akira |editor2-last=Nihonmatsu |editor2-first=Yasuhiro |editor3-last=Tokuda |editor3-first=Kazuo}} {{in lang|ja}} *{{cite thesis |type=PhD |last1=Grumbach |first1=Lisa |title=Sacrifice and Salvation in Medieval Japan: Hunting and Meat in Religious Practice at Suwa Jinja |date=2005 |publisher=Stanford University}} *{{cite book |author=J. [[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q9150392]] Wikidata name: Yasakatome [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:29, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Japanese deity}} {{Expand Japanese|八坂刀売神}} {{Infobox deity | type = Deity ([[Kunitsukami]], Senior First Rank) | name = Yasakatome
{{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|WD=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|WD=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. Stories and claims about the goddess are diverse and contradictory. Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼). Gakuseisha. p. 48, cited in Kanai (1982). p. 6. == See also == *{{ill|Takeminakata|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeminakata|qq=}} * {{ill|Tenshirakami|ja|天白神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenshirakami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天白信仰|1=Tenpaku faith|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3616095}} * {{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|qq=}} * [[Azumi people]] ==References== {{reflist}} == Bibliography == {{refbegin|30em|qq=draft}} *{{cite book |last=Ashkenazi |first=Michael |url=https://archive.org/details/handbookofjapane0000ashk |title=Handbook of Japanese Mythology |date=2003 |publisher=ABC-CLIO |isbn=978-1-57607-467-1 |url-access=registration}} *{{cite book |last1=Aston |first1=George |url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Nihongi:_Chronicles_of_Japan_from_the_Earliest_Times_to_A.D._697 |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697 |date=1896 |publisher=Kegan Paul, Trench, Trübner & Co. |location=London}} *{{cite book |last1=Chamberlain |first1=Basil (trans.) |url=http://sacred-texts.com/shi/kj/index.htm |title=A Translation of the "Ko-Ji-Ki," or "Records of Ancient Matters" |date=1882 |publisher=Lane, Crawford & Co. |location=Yokohama}} *{{cite book |title=諏訪信仰の中世―神話・伝承・歴史 (Suwa shinkō no chūsei: shinwa, denshō, rekishi) |date=2015 |publisher=Miyai Shoten |isbn=978-4838232888 |editor1-last=Fukuda |editor1-first=Akira |editor2-last=Nihonmatsu |editor2-first=Yasuhiro |editor3-last=Tokuda |editor3-first=Kazuo}} {{in lang|ja}} *{{cite thesis |type=PhD |last1=Grumbach |first1=Lisa |title=Sacrifice and Salvation in Medieval Japan: Hunting and Meat in Religious Practice at Suwa Jinja |date=2005 |publisher=Stanford University}} *{{cite book |author=J. Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼). {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|WD=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|WD=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. [[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] [[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q9150392]] Wikidata name: Yasakatome [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:29, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Japanese deity}} {{Expand Japanese|八坂刀売神}} {{Infobox deity | type = Deity ([[Kunitsukami]], Senior First Rank) | name = Yasakatome
{{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|WD=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|WD=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. Stories and claims about the goddess are diverse and contradictory. Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼). [[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] [[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] [[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q9150392]] Wikidata name: Yasakatome [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:29, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Japanese deity}} {{Expand Japanese|八坂刀売神}} {{Infobox deity | type = Deity ([[Kunitsukami]], Senior First Rank) | name = Yasakatome
{{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|WD=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|WD=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. Stories and claims about the goddess are diverse and contradictory. Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼). Gakuseisha. p. 48, cited in Kanai (1982). p. 6. == See also == *{{ill|Takeminakata|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeminakata|qq=}} * {{ill|Tenshirakami|ja|天白神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenshirakami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天白信仰|1=Tenpaku faith|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3616095}} * {{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|qq=}} * [[Azumi people]] ==References== {{reflist}} == Bibliography == {{refbegin|30em|qq=draft}} *{{cite book |last=Ashkenazi |first=Michael |url=https://archive.org/details/handbookofjapane0000ashk |title=Handbook of Japanese Mythology |date=2003 |publisher=ABC-CLIO |isbn=978-1-57607-467-1 |url-access=registration}} *{{cite book |last1=Aston |first1=George |url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Nihongi:_Chronicles_of_Japan_from_the_Earliest_Times_to_A.D._697 |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697 |date=1896 |publisher=Kegan Paul, Trench, Trübner & Co. |location=London}} *{{cite book |last1=Chamberlain |first1=Basil (trans.) |url=http://sacred-texts.com/shi/kj/index.htm |title=A Translation of the "Ko-Ji-Ki," or "Records of Ancient Matters" |date=1882 |publisher=Lane, Crawford & Co. |location=Yokohama}} *{{cite book |title=諏訪信仰の中世―神話・伝承・歴史 (Suwa shinkō no chūsei: shinwa, denshō, rekishi) |date=2015 |publisher=Miyai Shoten |isbn=978-4838232888 |editor1-last=Fukuda |editor1-first=Akira |editor2-last=Nihonmatsu |editor2-first=Yasuhiro |editor3-last=Tokuda |editor3-first=Kazuo}} {{in lang|ja}} *{{cite thesis |type=PhD |last1=Grumbach |first1=Lisa |title=Sacrifice and Salvation in Medieval Japan: Hunting and Meat in Religious Practice at Suwa Jinja |date=2005 |publisher=Stanford University}} *{{cite book |author=J. {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|WD=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|WD=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. Stories and claims about the goddess are diverse and contradictory. Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼). Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼). {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|WD=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|WD=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. [[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] [[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] [[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q9150392]] Wikidata name: Yasakatome [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:29, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Japanese deity}} {{Expand Japanese|八坂刀売神}} {{Infobox deity | type = Deity ([[Kunitsukami]], Senior First Rank) | name = Yasakatome
{{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|WD=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|WD=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. Stories and claims about the goddess are diverse and contradictory. Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼). [[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] [[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] [[en:Yasakatome]][[ja:八坂刀売神]][[simple:Yasakatome]][[zh:八坂刀賣神]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q9150392]] Wikidata name: Yasakatome [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:29, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Japanese deity}} {{Expand Japanese|八坂刀売神}} {{Infobox deity | type = Deity ([[Kunitsukami]], Senior First Rank) | name = Yasakatome
{{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|WD=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|WD=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. Stories and claims about the goddess are diverse and contradictory. Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼). Gakuseisha. p. 48, cited in Kanai (1982). p. 6. == See also == *{{ill|Takeminakata|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeminakata|qq=}} * {{ill|Tenshirakami|ja|天白神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenshirakami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天白信仰|1=Tenpaku faith|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3616095}} * {{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|qq=}} * [[Azumi people]] ==References== {{reflist}} == Bibliography == {{refbegin|30em|qq=draft}} *{{cite book |last=Ashkenazi |first=Michael |url=https://archive.org/details/handbookofjapane0000ashk |title=Handbook of Japanese Mythology |date=2003 |publisher=ABC-CLIO |isbn=978-1-57607-467-1 |url-access=registration}} *{{cite book |last1=Aston |first1=George |url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Nihongi:_Chronicles_of_Japan_from_the_Earliest_Times_to_A.D._697 |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697 |date=1896 |publisher=Kegan Paul, Trench, Trübner & Co. |location=London}} *{{cite book |last1=Chamberlain |first1=Basil (trans.) |url=http://sacred-texts.com/shi/kj/index.htm |title=A Translation of the "Ko-Ji-Ki," or "Records of Ancient Matters" |date=1882 |publisher=Lane, Crawford & Co. |location=Yokohama}} *{{cite book |title=諏訪信仰の中世―神話・伝承・歴史 (Suwa shinkō no chūsei: shinwa, denshō, rekishi) |date=2015 |publisher=Miyai Shoten |isbn=978-4838232888 |editor1-last=Fukuda |editor1-first=Akira |editor2-last=Nihonmatsu |editor2-first=Yasuhiro |editor3-last=Tokuda |editor3-first=Kazuo}} {{in lang|ja}} *{{cite thesis |type=PhD |last1=Grumbach |first1=Lisa |title=Sacrifice and Salvation in Medieval Japan: Hunting and Meat in Religious Practice at Suwa Jinja |date=2005 |publisher=Stanford University}} *{{cite book |author=J. {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}} | deity_of = God of water, agriculture, hot springs, nation building | member_of = | image = Suwa Taisha (Shimosha, Kaguraden) - panoramio.jpg | alt = | caption = [[Suwa-taisha]] Shimosha Akimiya Hall | other_names = {{lang|ja|姫大明神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀売神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂斗女命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂比売命}}, {{lang|ja|八坂刀自神}}, {{lang|ja|八坂入姫命 等}} | avatar_birth = | avatar_end = | mantra = | mantra benefits = | adherents = | height = | age = | tree = | day = | color = | number = | consort =[[Takeminakata]]; {{ill|Takeminakata|WD=Q9150391}}| parents =Unclear ([[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]] or Amayasakahiko no Mikoto); {{ill|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187}}| children = Izuhayao, Katakurabe, etc. | siblings = | region = | ethnic_group = | festivals = | cult_center = [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Kamisha Maemiya, Tsumashina Shrine | gender= {{ill|female|WD=Q6581072}} | offspring= {{ill|Q70537095|WD=Q70537095}} }} {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]'''|八坂刀売神}} is a [[kami]] in [[Shinto]]. She is worshipped in the [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] network of shrines.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-22 |title=Suwa Shinkō {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |access-date=2023-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522035213/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8881 |archive-date=2023-05-22 }} She is the spouse of [[Takeminakata]] and most often considered to be the deity of the Lower Shrine of Suwa or the ''Shimosha''.Muraoka (1969). pp. 5–6. Unlike the relatively well-documented Suwa ''Kamisha'', very little concrete information is available regarding the origins of the ''Shimosha'' and its goddess.Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696. At Suwa Taisha Takeminakata is enshrined at Hon Miya and Yasakatome is enshrined in Mae Miya.{{Cite journal |last=Gerbert |first=Elaine |date=1996 |title=The Suwa Pillar Festival Revisited |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2719402 |journal=Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=325 |doi=10.2307/2719402 |jstor=2719402 |issn=0073-0548}} She is considered to be the concubine of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Kami]], the enshrined deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Shrine, and is enshrined at Suwa Taisha Shitasha and Suwa Shrines in various places. Yasakatome's first historical attestation is in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'', where the goddess is given the Rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) by the imperial court in the tenth month of [[:en:Jōwa (Heian period)|Jōwa]] 9 (842 CE), five months after the same Rank was conferred on Takeminakata.{{cite web |title=續日本後紀 |url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/shokukouki.html |website=J－TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館}}{{cite web |title=南方刀美神社二座（八坂刀売命神） |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=240201 |website=神社資料データベース (Shinto Jinja Database) |publisher=Kokugakuin University}} She is not found in the [[Kojiki]] or the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihonshoki]]. As Takeminakata rose up in Rank, so did Yasakatome,Miyasaka (1987). pp. 37-38.{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第二}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' (日本文德天皇實錄)|wslink=zh:日本文德天皇實錄|chapter=卷第三}}{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十}} so that by 867 CE, Yasakatome had been promoted to senior second (正二位).{{cite wikisource|plaintitle=''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (日本三代實錄)|wslink=zh:日本三代實錄|chapter=卷第十四}} The goddess was finally promoted to senior first Rank (正一位) in 1074 ([[:en:Jōhō|Jōhō]] 1).Ōwa (1990). p. 221-223. Stories and claims about the goddess are diverse and contradictory. Regarding her parentage for instance, the lore of Kawaai Shrine (川会神社) in [[:en:Kitaazumi District|Kitaazumi District]] identifies Yasakatome as the daughter of [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]], god of the sea,{{cite web |title=八坂刀売神（ヤサカトメノカミ |url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625160608/http://japangod.dip.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%9D%82%E5%88%80%E5%A3%B2%E7%A5%9E.html |archive-date=June 25, 2017 |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)}} which has been seen as hinting to a connection between the goddess and the seafaring [[Azumi people|Azumi clan]] ([[:ja:阿曇氏|安曇氏]]).Miyasaka (1987). p. 39. Another claim originating from sources dating from the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] is that Yasakatome was the daughter of Ame-no-yasakahiko (天八坂彦命), a god recorded in the ''Kuji Hongi'' as one of the companions of [[List of Japanese deities#Minor kami|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto]] when the latter came down from heaven.{{cite book |last1=Ponsonby-Fane |first1=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UVO4AwAAQBAJ&pg=PT148 |title=Studies in Shinto & Shrines |date=2014 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1136893018}}{{cite web |title=先代舊事本紀卷第三 天神本紀 |url=https://miko.org/~uraki/kuon/furu/text/sendaikuji/sendaikuji03.htm |website=私本 先代舊事本紀}} Local [[Shinto]] tradition of [[:en:Lake Suwa|Lake Suwa]] holds that the ridges are formed by the gods crossing the lake when traveling between the various buildings of the [[:en:Suwa Grand Shrine|Suwa Grand Shrine]]. Folklore says it is the guardian god of Suwa, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-kami]], leaving his sanctuary to meet with his wife, the goddess Yasakatome, joining the opposite bank by walking on frozen water.{{cite web |last1=Takahiro |first1=Nogami |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Shrines and Cultic Practices : Suwa Shinkō |url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1080 |accessdate=25 October 2020 |website=eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp}} The ice cracks that appear on Lake Suwa during cold winters, the ''omiwatari'' ([[Takeminakata#Omiwatari|see above]]) are reputed in folklore to be caused by Suwa Myōjin's crossing the frozen lake to visit Yasakatome.{{cite book |author=Japan. Dept. of railways |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smA0AAAAMAAJ |title=The Hot Springs of Japan (and the Principal Cold Springs) Including Chosen (Korea) Taiwan (Formosa) South Manchuria, Together with Many Tables Giving Classification, Chemical Basis, Curative Values, Radio-activity, Etc. 196 Illustrations, 15 Maps, Specially Drawn, 2 Colored Lithographs |year=1922 |page=194}} An alternative explanation for the word ''-tomi'' (as well as the ''-tome'' in 'Yasakatome', the name of this god's consort) is to link it with dialectal words for "snake" (''tomi'', ''tobe'', or ''tōbe''), thereby seeing the name as hinting to the god being a kind of [[:en:Snake worship|serpentine]] water deity (''[[mizuchi]]'').Tomiku, Takashi (1970). ''Himiko'' (卑弥呼).
